title: Generator Maintenance Log Form
subtitle: An original generator workflow that carries planned or condition-based maintenance through safe release, with explicit qualified-review, stop-work, escalation, and accountable handoff controls.
description: A workflow-complete generator maintenance log form for the standby or prime generator system that captures exact identity, domain observations, supporting evidence, decisions, exceptions, responsible owners, and closeout without replacing professional judgment or the organization's controlling procedures.
use_case: Use when service personnel need one record for maintenance trigger, asset baseline, work-control references, recurring events, readings, deferred defects, and qualified return-to-service approval. The generator service coordinator owns routing, and closure requires documented evidence, disposition of restrictions, and acceptance by the designated reviewer.

sections.title: Generator maintenance log identity and ownership
sections.guidance: Define the maintained system, service interval, operating owner, and review period.

sections.title: Generator asset baseline and maintenance readiness
sections.guidance: Reconcile the exact asset and known condition before maintenance or testing begins.

blocks.label: Planned maintenance task set
items: Confirm generator, engine, controller, battery, fuel, and ATS identities
Coordinate affected loads, outage limits, and run or transfer authorization
Establish hazardous-energy, start-prevention, exhaust, and access controls
Inspect fuel, lubrication, cooling, intake, exhaust, battery, and charging systems
Complete approved filters, fluids, belts, hoses, terminals, or cleaning work
Record controller alarms, hours, settings, and maintenance indicators
Perform authorized start, run, load, and transfer checks
Record oil pressure, temperature, voltage, frequency, load, and battery values
Correct labels, housekeeping, leaks, and deficiencies within approved scope
Return unit to approved mode and hand off limitations to the site owner

sections.title: Generator work control and safe service boundary
sections.guidance: Record the qualified roles and controlling references; do not use this log as the controlling procedure.

blocks.label: Service readiness confirmations
items: Current procedure, manufacturer information, and applicable requirements were reviewed
Asset boundaries, every energy source, and affected systems were identified
Authorized, affected, contractor, and operations roles were coordinated
Isolation, stored-energy control, and verification references are complete
Required tools, instruments, parts, and protective controls are available
Test, temporary energization, and return-to-service steps have explicit authority
Customer, public, traffic, environmental, and critical-service impacts are controlled
Stop conditions and emergency escalation path are understood

blocks.label: Maintenance stop-work boundary
blocks.guidance: This form is not a generator energy-control, energized-work, or transfer authorization. Stop for fuel leaks, exhaust or carbon-monoxide concerns, fire, heat, arcing, unexpected start, exposed moving parts, or unknown backfeed. Qualified and authorized personnel must control isolation, test conditions, affected loads, and return to automatic service under current site procedures. Maintenance stays restricted when isolation, stored energy, system condition, or work scope is unknown. Only the designated authorized person may direct changes to controls and the qualified release owner may approve return to service.

sections.title: Generator maintenance events, condition, and readings
sections.guidance: Create a traceable history of work completed, condition found, evidence, and deferred action.

fields.label: Wear pattern, recurring fault, consumable trend, configuration change, and supporting evidence

sections.title: Generator exceptions, stop conditions, and escalation
sections.guidance: Make every unresolved condition visible with an immediate control, owner, due point, and final disposition.

blocks.label: Stop-condition screen
items: Fuel, oil, coolant, exhaust, or battery leak
Carbon-monoxide alarm, exhaust intrusion, or ventilation failure
Smoke, fire, abnormal heat, burning odor, or electrical arcing
Unexpected start, automatic operation, transfer, or backfeed risk
Exposed moving part, damaged guard, severe vibration, or loose component
Uncontrolled stored electrical, mechanical, thermal, or fluid energy
Critical-load interruption without site and operations authorization
Test or repair beyond the assigned qualified person's scope
blocks.guidance: Check any condition observed or reported; checking an item does not mean the condition is controlled.

blocks.label: Qualified-person and stop-work boundary
blocks.guidance: This form is not a generator energy-control, energized-work, or transfer authorization. Stop for fuel leaks, exhaust or carbon-monoxide concerns, fire, heat, arcing, unexpected start, exposed moving parts, or unknown backfeed. Qualified and authorized personnel must control isolation, test conditions, affected loads, and return to automatic service under current site procedures.

blocks.label: Exception and escalation register
blocks.guidance: Link each maintenance exception to supporting evidence and keep it open until disposition is recorded.

sections.title: Generator decision, handoff, and accountable closeout
sections.guidance: Record the decision, remaining limitations, next action, and the people accountable for acceptance.

blocks.label: Closeout completeness
items: Standby or prime generator system identity and location were reconciled
Observed facts, measurements, and evidence references are complete
Decision authority and applicable review requirements were confirmed
Stop conditions, restrictions, and open exceptions remain visible
Customer, operations, or site handoff was recorded
Next action, owner, due point, and record-retention route are explicit

fields.label: Limitations, assumptions, restrictions, customer message, and next-action context

blocks.label: Accountable review and handoff
blocks.guidance: Signatures acknowledge the recorded decision and handoff; they do not waive unresolved restrictions.
